title: COPD exacerbation with heart failure of unstated type and acuity
discharge_summary: SYNTHETIC CASE - NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient: Synthetic Patient 02, 68-year-old female. MRN: SYN-0002
Reason for admission: Worsening shortness of breath, wheezing, and leg swelling for 5 days.
Past medical history: COPD (former smoker, quit 2015), heart failure, hypertension, hyperlipidemia.
The patient was admitted with a COPD exacerbation and treated with nebulized albuterol and ipratropium, IV methylprednisolone, and doxycycline.

On admission she had 3+ bilateral pitting edema to the knees and bibasilar crackles. Chest x-ray showed pulmonary vascular congestion and small bilateral pleural effusions. BNP was 1,450 pg/mL. Echocardiogram on hospital day 2 showed left ventricular ejection fraction of 25-30% with global hypokinesis.
She was given IV furosemide 40 mg twice daily for 3 days with 3.2 kg net weight loss, then changed to oral furosemide 40 mg daily. Edema improved to trace by discharge.
Wheezing resolved and she was weaned to room air on hospital day 3.
Discharge plan: Prednisone taper, doxycycline to complete 5 days, furosemide 40 mg daily, follow up with cardiology in 1 week.

expected.notes: Heart failure is documented without type or acuity. EF 25-30%, BNP 1,450, congestion on x-ray, and IV diuresis point to acute (or acute on chronic) systolic heart failure (I50.21/I50.23, MCC). Query for type and acuity.
